seoDescription: Master the essential setup for your FastAPI projects in VS Code. This guide walks you through verifying your Python installation, creating a project folder, and setting up an isolated virtual environment (`venv`) to manage dependencies. Learn to install FastAPI and the Uvicorn web server using pip. The tutorial also covers the optional but recommended step of configuring a React front end by downloading a starter project from GitHub, installing NodeJS dependencies with `npm install`, and running the development server.

chapters.description: Learn how to verify your Python version from the terminal, which is the first prerequisite for starting with FastAPI.

chapters.description: Understand the optional requirement of NodeJS for running the React front end and how to check your version or download it.

chapters.title: IDE Setup: VS Code and Extensions
chapters.description: This chapter covers setting up your Integrated Development Environment, recommending VS Code and the essential Python extension from Microsoft.

chapters.title: Downloading the Front-End Project from GitHub
chapters.description: Follow the steps to download the starter front-end code from a GitHub repository, unzip it, and move the 'frontend' folder into your new project directory.

chapters.title: Installing Dependencies and Running the React App
chapters.description: Learn how to open your project in VS Code, navigate to the front-end directory, and use 'npm install' and 'npm start' to run the React application.

chapters.title: Introducing Virtual Environments
chapters.description: Discover why isolating project dependencies is crucial and learn the purpose of a Python virtual environment to avoid global package installations.

chapters.title: Creating and Activating a Virtual Environment
chapters.description: This section demonstrates the command to create a new virtual environment and shows how to activate and deactivate it within your terminal.

chapters.title: Installing FastAPI and Uvicorn
chapters.description: Walk through the final setup step: installing the FastAPI framework and the Uvicorn ASGI server into your activated virtual environment using pip.

summary:
## Core Prerequisites
- **Python**: Verify your installation and version by running `python --version` in your terminal. Versions 3.12 and 3.13 are confirmed to work.
- **Node.js (Optional)**: This is only required if you want to run the provided React front-end application. Check your version with `node --version`.
- **IDE**: The video uses **VS Code**, but any modern code editor or IDE like PyCharm will work.
- **VS Code Extension**: If using VS Code, ensure you have the official **Python** extension from Microsoft installed.

## Initial Project Setup
1.  Create a main project folder on your local machine (e.g., `fast-api-demo-recording`).
2.  Download the front-end source code from the specified GitHub repository.
    > [!TIP]
    > It's recommended to **download the ZIP** file rather than cloning the repository. This makes it easier to isolate and copy only the `frontend` folder that you need.
3.  Move the extracted `frontend` folder into your main project folder.

## Front-End (React App) Setup
This section is optional if you plan to interact with your API using tools like Postman, Insomnia, or the built-in Swagger UI.
- To run the React front end:
    1. Open a terminal and navigate into the `frontend` directory: `cd frontend`.
    2. Install all the necessary dependencies defined in `package.json` by running: `npm install`. This command creates a `node_modules` folder.
    3. Start the local development server with: `npm start`.
    > [!NOTE]
    > The web application will likely show a "Connection refused" error. This is expected, as the FastAPI back-end server is not yet running.

## Back-End (FastAPI) Setup

### Why Use a Virtual Environment?
- A **virtual environment** is a critical tool for isolating project dependencies. 
- Without one, `pip install` adds packages to your global Python installation, which can cause version conflicts between different projects.

### Creating and Using a Virtual Environment
1.  **Create the environment**: From your project's root directory, run the following command. The name `my_env` can be changed to whatever you prefer.
    ```bash
    python -m venv my_env
    ```
2.  **Activate the environment**: Before installing packages, you must activate the environment. The command varies by operating system and shell. For PowerShell (as shown in the video):
    ```powershell
    .\my_env\Scripts\Activate.ps1
    ```
    > [!IMPORTANT]
    > A successfully activated environment is indicated by its name appearing in your terminal prompt, e.g., `(my_env) C:\...>`.
3.  **Deactivate the environment**: When you are finished working in the environment, you can exit it by running the `deactivate` command.

### Installing FastAPI and Uvicorn
- With your virtual environment **activated**, you can now install the required Python packages:
  ```bash
  pip install fastapi uvicorn
  ```
- **FastAPI** is the core web framework for building the API.
- **Uvicorn** is the high-performance ASGI (Asynchronous Server Gateway Interface) server that will run your FastAPI application.
- You can confirm a successful installation by running `pip list`, which will now show `fastapi`, `uvicorn`, and their dependencies within the isolated environment.
